name: ICMM homepage: news and report summaries on mining standards
title: ICMM homepage: news and report summaries on mining standards
answer: This is the ICMM homepage, a leadership organisation for responsibly produced minerals and metals. It is a landing page of news items and report summaries rather than a single detailed study. The most useful thing for AI in mining is that it points to ICMM's work on safety data, tailings standards, water risk, greenhouse gas emissions and tax contributions, and says modern mining is built on innovation, rigorous standards and safety. It does not itself describe artificial intelligence or automated monitoring in detail.

sections.body: The International Council on Mining and Metals publishes this page. It is the ICMM homepage, a landing page that collects news items, report summaries and announcements rather than a single detailed document. Its scope includes safety, water, greenhouse gas emissions, tax, tailings management, appointments and a documentary. The text was harvested on 26 September 2026 and refers to 2025 reports and events in 2026.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: ICMM describes itself as a leadership organisation working for a safe, just and sustainable world enabled by responsibly produced minerals and metals. The page highlights Danielle Martin discussing why social performance capability is reaching an inflection point and why investment in people, leadership and expertise matters now. It notes that ICMM's 2025 safety report provides transparent data on fatalities, injuries and workplace hazards to help drive learning and continual improvement across the industry. It says water may be the missing piece in the energy transition, with Emma Gagen arguing that future mineral supply depends on more than permitting and supply chains. An ICMM report maps where mining and metals facilities intersect with water stress, depletion, drought, flood and interannual variability risks. ICMM published a new Global Mining & Metals Greenhouse Gas Emissions Dataset, which puts mining and metals emissions in perspective as demand for energy transition minerals grows. The 2025 Tax Contribution Report shows members paid a higher share of earnings to society despite lower profits, underscoring mining's role in public revenues. The page also mentions a documentary premiere on 10 February 2026 about 55 runners completing a marathon 1,119 metres below sea level in Boliden's Garpenberg mine in Sweden, and says modern mining done well is built on innovation, rigorous standards and a relentless focus on safety. It notes the Tailings Progress Report on company members implementing the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management, and announces Iván Arriagada as Chair for a two-year term and James Clark as Director of Communications and External Affairs from March 2026.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives these specifics: ICMM's 2025 safety report covers fatalities, injuries and workplace hazards; the 2025 Tax Contribution Report says members paid a higher share of earnings to society despite lower profits; the Global Mining & Metals Greenhouse Gas Emissions Dataset is described as putting mining and metals emissions in perspective; the water risk report maps intersections with water stress, depletion, drought, flood and interannual variability; the Tailings Progress Report covers implementation of the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management; the documentary premiere is on 10 February 2026 and follows 55 runners completing a marathon 1,119 metres below sea level in Boliden's Garpenberg mine in Sweden; Iván Arriagada is appointed Chair for a two-year term; James Clark becomes Director of Communications and External Affairs in March 2026.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in mining would use this source mainly as a pointer to ICMM's standards and reporting work, including safety data, tailings management, water risk, greenhouse gas emissions and tax contributions. It shows the industry body's current priorities and the reports it publishes. However, the source text does not discuss artificial intelligence, automation or digital transformation, so it cannot support claims about those topics. It is useful for context on the standards and data landscape that AI in mining might relate to, but not for evidence of AI adoption or automated safety monitoring.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Mining

sections.body: This is a landing page, not a full report, so it gives headlines and short summaries rather than detailed methods, data or analysis. It does not cover artificial intelligence, automation, digital transformation or automated safety monitoring. It is published by ICMM, an industry leadership organisation, so it is an industry body source rather than an independent or peer reviewed study. It is partial and time bound, harvested on 26 September 2026, and it mixes 2025 reports with 2026 announcements and events. The text also does not provide the underlying data for the safety, tax, water or emissions reports it mentions.
